summary: Map ~32 reported Chatyy bugs/features across 12 parallel investigators + synthesize a prioritized fix triage

items.title: iOS Share Extension iCloud Photo Hang — No Progress or Timeout Feedback
items.currentState: ShareViewController uses NSItemProvider.loadFileRepresentation to download iCloud photos. When image is hosted in iCloud, user sees blank Preparando spinner for up to 20 seconds. If download stalls or network is slow, no progress visible, no error message, and no cancel option. User perceives app as stuck loading.
items.rootCause: loadFileRepresentation has a hard 20s timeout but no user-facing progress or timeout UI. No fallback strategy if iCloud download fails. No per-chunk retry logic. Progress.fractionCompleted is observed internally but not displayed to user.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp iOS share extension: (1) Shows real iCloud download percent as Progress.fractionCompleted ticks, not opaque spinner; (2) 15-30 second timeout with explicit message at 10s; (3) Tap-to-cancel dismisses in-flight requests; (4) Fallback to low-res UIImage if network stalls; (5) Exponential backoff retry logic.
items.fixPlan: STEP 1: Display real download percent in UI instead of spinner. Observe Progress.fractionCompleted via KVO and update label: iCloud: 45%. STEP 2: Add dual-timeout gate: soft timeout at 10s shows Cancel dialog, hard timeout at 20s auto-dismisses + error. STEP 3: Call Progress.cancel() when user taps cancel to abort CKAsset request. STEP 4: Fallback for stalled downloads — if timeout fires on weak network, attempt UIImage decode via ImageIO.kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways (downsampling to 256pt). STEP 5: Add exponential backoff on retry — 2^(attempt-1) second waits. STEP 6: Surface three error codes: timeout=iCloud demorando, network=Sem internet, unavailable=Imagem nao disponivel.

items.title: Short Video Note Loses Circular Shape After Send — Type Normalization Bug
items.currentState: User records 60-second video note. Optimistic bubble renders circular (300x300, mute button) with type=video_note. After upload and backend sync, message type becomes video and bubble renders rectangular via ChatMediaViewer. Circular RoundVideoViewer never opens.
items.rootCause: Message type field not preserved through send+receive. Backend chat.php normalizes type based on MIME or extension, overwriting explicit video_note type. Message syncs back with type=video. renderMessage checks type===video and uses rectangular path, never hitting video_note case.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp preserves type=video_note end-to-end: stored in message DB, sent to receivers, rendering always checks type first. If video_note, use circular 320x320 player. If video, use rectangular fullscreen. Type is permanent message property, never lost after send.
items.fixPlan: STEP 1 (Frontend): Verify handleSendVideoNote sets type=video_note in optimisticMsg and savePendingMessage — already correct. STEP 2 (API): Ensure chatUploadFile passes fileType parameter to backend. STEP 3 (Backend): In chat.php INSERT, check if client sent explicit type field in upload payload. If present and valid, use it. DO NOT override with MIME-inferred type. SQL: INSERT INTO chat_messages (type) VALUES (COALESCE(request.type, INFER_TYPE(...))). STEP 4 (Frontend receive): Preserve type field from WS messages exactly as sent — no re-normalization. STEP 5 (Rendering): In renderMessage(), check case video_note BEFORE fallback case video. STEP 6 (Testing): Verify chat_messages.type=video_note in backend DB after send.

items.title: Status music: only shows song NAME, doesn't play audio; can't trim/select which portion of track plays
items.currentState: StatusCamera.js (line 245) captures musicTrack as {id, title} and passes it to onCapture. StoryViewer.js (line 732-758) has StatusMusicPlayer component that creates audio player from music_preview_url, but only plays if URL exists. Backend stores only music_title, music_artist, music_preview_url, music_cover_url in status_create call (api.js:4790-4795). No offset/start_time stored. Profile.js and app screens show music name as text pill but never integrated real playback. StatusCamera music picker loads from Pixabay (chat_status_music_search API call) but NO trim/scrub UI exposed to user.
items.rootCause: 1) expo-av removed in SDK 55 — old require('expo-av').Audio threw unhandled error, so _StatusAudio stayed null and nothing played. 2) No start_offset / trim_seconds fields in database schema or API contract. 3) No scrub timeline UI in StatusCamera music picker. 4) Music only plays in StoryViewer, not in composer preview.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp Status music: user picks song, then scrubs timeline via white handle over waveform or taps white dots on seek bar (auto-jumps to popular sections). Supports 15-60s depending on photo/video. Stores start_offset timestamp in backend. Instagram Stories: similar UI with slider at bottom showing duration (5-15s for photos), white handle on waveform to scrub forward/backward and select exact lyrics/portion. Both use preview_url + start_offset fields to resume playback at chosen position.
items.fixPlan: 1) Migrate expo-av → expo-audio (SDK 55 compatible): change require from 'expo-av' to 'expo-audio', update player API (createAudioPlayer instead of Audio.Sound). 2) Add database columns to chat_user_status: music_start_ms (offset in milliseconds where track should begin). 3) Add trim UI to StatusCamera music picker: horizontal timeline with duration label (15s for photo, 60s for video) + draggable handle to set start position. Pass music_start_ms in onCapture → statusPublish → status_create API. 4) Fetch full song duration from Pixabay metadata, render waveform background (visual feedback). 5) Update StatusMusicPlayer to read music_start_ms from status meta, seek player to that offset on load. 6) Backend: in status_create endpoint, validate music_start_ms + duration <= full track duration.

items.title: Highlights (Destaques) on profile load VERY slowly and don't function like Instagram
items.currentState: Profile.js (line 1157-1202) fetches statusHighlightList on mount, sets highlightsLoading=true during fetch, then renders HighlightEditSheet/HighlightShareSheet modals on demand. HighlightEditSheet.js (line 67-87) loads items + stories + stats with Promise.all 3 endpoints. No pagination — loads ALL highlights every mount. No caching between profile views. FlatList rendering ~100 tiles in a single ScrollView without windowing. No skeleton loader during fetch. Backend status_highlight_list returns full item count per highlight but no lazy load cursor.
items.rootCause: 1) N+1 query: profile_get doesn't return highlights; forces separate statusHighlightList call. 2) No pagination cursor / limit in backend endpoint. 3) No SWR/cache — refetch on every Profile open. 4) HighlightEditSheet loads 3 endpoints in series (not cached), blocking UI. 5) FlatList of 100+ thumbnail tiles in ScrollView = O(n) render cost, no virtualization.
items.whatsappPattern: Instagram Highlights: 1) Highlight strip at top of profile (circular tiles, auto-scroll left/right). 2) Tap highlight → full-screen modal with swipe-through carousel of statuses. 3) Edit icon → bottom sheet with rename field + cover picker + item list. 4) Highlights load FAST: backend returns highlights list with item count + cover_url only (NOT full item details). 5) Items lazy-load when user opens the highlight carousel (separate endpoint with pagination). 6) Visual feedback: skeleton shimmer while loading. 7) Smooth scroll with momentum; highlight strip is a horizontal FlatList (windowed).
items.fixPlan: 1) Add LIMIT 50 + cursor-based pagination to backend status_highlight_list endpoint. Return {id, title, cover_url, active_count, created_at} per highlight (NO status_ids array). 2) Wire SWR cache in useHighlights hook (new) — dedup repeated profile opens. 3) Create separate statusHighlightItems endpoint (with pagination) that HighlightEditSheet calls on open. 4) Replace HighlightEditSheet's Promise.all with sequential load: 1) fetch items (paginated), 2) fetch stats async in background. 5) Horizontal FlatList for highlights strip in Profile, with FlatList windowing (removeClippedSubviews=true, updateCellsBatchingPeriod=50). 6) Add skeleton loader for highlights strip (4 shimmer circles) and edit sheet (tile grid placeholder). 7) Unify highlight open → opens modal (same as StoryViewer carousel), not separate HighlightEditSheet for viewing.

items.title: Viewing own status from profile causes profile screen to remount and flicker
items.currentState: Profile.js renders <StoryRingAvatar> wrapping <StoryViewer>. When StoryViewer modal closes (onClose→setViewingStoryEmail(null)), parent Profile re-renders. StoryRingAvatar re-mounts because it re-creates the StoryViewer Modal on every render (no memoization). Each StoryViewer open re-fetches status_list via useStatuses. No stale status cache between open/close cycles.
items.rootCause: 1) Profile doesn't memoize StoryRingAvatar children → re-creates component on every parent render. 2) StoryViewer not wrapped in React.memo. 3) useStatuses hook refetches on every mount instead of using cache. 4) No key stability for status carousel items → React re-mounts entire tree.
items.whatsappPattern: Instagram profile: tapping story ring opens modal without profile screen visibly reloading. Modal is Portal'ed (top-level in tree), separate from profile scroll context. Profile stays mounted + visible underneath with opacity 0.5 (slight dim). Close modal → profile still at exact same scroll position. No flicker, no re-paint of profile content.
items.fixPlan: 1) Wrap StoryViewer in React.memo (no props change between open/close). 2) Memoize StoryRingAvatar render in Profile.js to prevent re-creation. 3) Move StoryViewer Modal out of Profile component tree → use React Portal at root level (RootNavigator or AppRoot). Open via context/ref instead of state. 4) Stabilize useStatuses cache: add fingerprint comparison (email + timestamp of latest status) so re-mount doesn't trigger refetch if data hasn't changed. 5) Force profile scroll position save on unmount, restore on remount (FlatList scrollToOffset). 6) Add FlatList windowSize={10} to status carousel so items outside viewport don't render.

items.title: Purple ring on profile should only appear if person has ACTIVE status (not expired/old)
items.currentState: StoryRingAvatar.js renders purple ring border if `hasStories` prop is truthy. hasStories passed from Profile.js (line 1684+) is set to `groups.length > 0 && groups.some(g => g.statuses && g.statuses.length > 0)`. This check does NOT filter out expired statuses. useStatuses hook fetches status_list from backend, which includes all statuses from last 24h, but no client-side expiry check. Backend status_list may include expired rows if cron cleanup is delayed.
items.rootCause: 1) Ring visibility gated on total status count, not active_count. 2) No expiry check in Profile.js or StoryRingAvatar. 3) Backend status_list endpoint doesn't exclude expired statuses (created_at < NOW - 24h). 4) useStatuses doesn't re-filter or validate created_at on fetch.
items.whatsappPattern: Instagram profile: ring only appears if user has ≥1 active (unexpired) story. Active = created_at + 24h > now. Backend status_list filters: created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'. Ring disappears immediately when last story expires (via cron OR client-side timestamp check). Visual feedback: no ring = no active stories, even if user posted stories in the past.
items.fixPlan: 1) Backend (chat.php status_list): add WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours' to filter query. OR add is_expired calculated column: (created_at + INTERVAL '24 hours') < NOW(). 2) Frontend Profile.js: add expiry check hasStories = groups.some(g => g.statuses?.some(s => isStatusActive(s))). isStatusActive = (s.created_at) => Date.now() - new Date(s.created_at) < 24*3600*1000. 3) StoryRingAvatar: only render ring border if hasStories && !isExpired. 4) useStatuses: on fetch, filter out expired statuses client-side as defensive measure: statuses.filter(s => isStatusActive(s)). 5) Add visual debug: if status.created_at + 24h < now, skip it silently (don't show in carousel, don't count for ring).

items.title: Block enforcement gaps: caller rings blocked user
items.currentState: Block filter in chat_send at line 5104 gates message insert in 1:1 chats only. Groups still broadcast to all non-blocking members. No block check in call_notify. Caller can call blocked callee who receives VoIP and FCM ring. No reverse check for blocked user ringing blocker back.
items.rootCause: call_notify loop at line 7880 checks callBlockedPeers only for BLOCKED_EMAIL equals caller. Never checks if CALLER is blocked by PEER. Bidirectional send check exists at line 5115 but call path omitted it.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp bidirectional block prevents BOTH directions from messaging or calling. If A blocks B neither A to B nor B to A send or ring
items.fixPlan: At call_notify line 7880 add reverse block check before loop to load all peers who have BLOCKED the caller. Skip peer if caller is in their blocklist. Add self-call guard at line 7880 to skip if strtolower pe equals strtolower user email

items.title: Push leak vectors: stale tokens, wrong-account pushes, logged-out devices
items.currentState: chat_send line 279 correctly filters sender from push recipients. fcmGetUserTokens filters tokens older than 60 days at line 1106. No check for logged-out users or token expiry beyond age. No way to revoke token on logout. Token stays in vhosts until 60d TTL
items.rootCause: Token cleanup is TIME-based 60 days not EVENT-based on logout. Old token never marked stale on logout so old device can still receive push after user logs in elsewhere. fcmRemoveInvalidToken only fires on FCM 404 error not proactively on logout
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp invalidates push token on logout via user agent deletion and backend stale mark. On re-login fresh token registered. 60d cleanup is safety net not primary mechanism
items.fixPlan: On logout in email.php call fcmRemoveInvalidToken with active_token PROACTIVELY not just on 404. Store current device token in session and remove immediately at logout. Keep 60d TTL as fallback for abandoned devices

items.title: E2EE Disabled by Default — Opt-In Only (Telegram Secret Chat Model)
items.currentState: E2EE is OFF by default for direct conversations. Lines 8789-8796 in /root/webmail-app/app/chat-conversation.js explicitly disable auto-enable: code checks conversation is_e2ee flag, but if NOT already enabled (and conversation is 'direct' type), it does NOTHING. Users must manually enable via menu → 'Chat secreto' (Secret Chat). Plaintext is the default path.
items.rootCause: Design decision to follow Telegram's opt-in model (not WhatsApp default-on). Code comment (lines 8790-8795) states: 'E2E is now OPT-IN only... Regular chats are server-side readable = works on any device. This eliminates the lock problem for 99% of users. E2E auto-enable DISABLED.'
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp uses Signal Protocol with 4-DH X3DH for initial key agreement + Double Ratchet for per-message forward secrecy. Identity keys (long-term), signed prekeys (medium-term ~30d rotation), one-time prekeys, and ephemeral keys per message. Multi-device handled via device_id registration. Sender Keys for groups. WhatsApp enables E2EE by default on ALL 1:1 conversations; Chatyy makes it opt-in to avoid multi-device 'lock' UX friction.
items.fixPlan: Stage 1 (P0): Flip default to ON for direct conversations. Remove the else-if block lines 8789-8796 that disables auto-enable. When conversation type='direct', call handleToggleE2E(true) if not already enabled. Stage 2 (P1): Surface E2EE enrollment in onboarding (not secret chats, but transparent lock icon). Stage 3 (P2): Implement device linking UI so users can unlock via Face ID on new devices (WhatsApp Web parity). Stage 4 (P3): Add 'restore from backup' flow when logging in on new device to avoid key rotation. Stage 5 (Safety): Roll out with QA: test 1:1 plaintext→encrypted upgrade, verify old messages remain readable, check group conversations stay optional.

items.title: Identity Key vs Device Key Misalignment — Silent Key Rotation on Multi-Device
items.currentState: Code uses TWO separate keypairs: (1) identity_key — long-term, scoped per-email, restored from server backup on new device. (2) device_key — per-install UUID, generated locally, NOT backed up (lines 264-312 in e2e.js). When user logs in on new phone, identity_key IS restored (avoiding rotation), BUT device_key is freshly generated. Problem: old messages encrypted FOR the old device_id become undecryptable on new phone because envelope routing keys off device_id.
items.rootCause: Device linking not fully implemented. chat.php has tables chat_pending_envelopes (per-device) + schema for device registration (lines 1592-1651), but no ClientEnvelopeDecrypt endpoint to re-encrypt envelopes for new device. Multi-device Stages 1-7 are implemented in task list (#1024-#1031) but Stage 5 (encrypted envelope per-device) is incomplete. Old v2/v3 envelopes target device_id implicitly via device bundle, but no mechanism to migrate when user adds/logs into new device.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp: Identity key is cross-device (synced via iCloud/Google backup encrypted with user password). Device key per phone is auto-registered. When user logs in on new device: restore identity, generate fresh device key, auto-re-encrypt pending envelopes via signal protocol ratcheting. Sender automatically fans out to all registered device_ids. Receiver's new device seamlessly decrypts because identity key (DH root) is the same, only device DH differs.
items.fixPlan: Stage 1: Add e2ee_device_publish endpoint (backend + frontend) to wire getDevicePublicKey() on every auth refresh (not just chat init). Stage 2: Implement chat_envelope_migrate backend endpoint — when new device detects it can't decrypt a v3 envelope (wrong device_id or missing session), it requests migration: server fans out re-encryption via sender's device + identity key. Stage 3: Cache device registrations locally (device_id → pub) to avoid round-trip on every send. Stage 4: QA multidevice: log in on Emulator 1, send encrypted msg, switch to Emulator 2, verify old msg readable (identity restored), can re-encrypt + forward, no 'chave indisponível' banner.

items.title: E2EE Kill-Switch for Calls (CALL_E2EE_ENABLED env var) — Default OFF, No Rollout Path
items.currentState: Three call E2EE endpoints (chat_call_invite_e2ee, chat_call_key_ack, chat_call_key_rotate) exist in chat.php (lines 27316-27330) but are DISABLED by default. Code checks getenv('CALL_E2EE_ENABLED')!=='1' and returns 501 'not enabled'. Separate kill-switch CALL_E2EE_KILLSWITCH can flip all three to 503 in <1 minute if rollout fails. No monitoring, no gradual rollout, no QA gate defined.
items.rootCause: Call E2EE is Phase 1 staged rollout infrastructure (lines 27325-27328 comment confirms 'Feature flag default OFF for Phase 1 staged rollout'). Never enabled in production. SDP fingerprint + envelope fan-out to call participants is coded but gated by env var. No frontend UI to offer encrypted calls, no backend metrics to track adoption if enabled.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp: Calls encrypted via same Signal protocol as chat. Identity key auth happens once at contact verification. Per-call ephemeral DH inside call signaling (ICE candidates, SDP mlines). Sender keys for group calls (fanout envelopes to all participants via SFU). No separate key exchange — reuses chat session key or derives from shared identity.
items.fixPlan: Stage 1: Add frontend Call E2EE toggle in call pre-dial screen (lock icon → 'Encrypted call' label). Backend checks is_e2ee + both users have keys registered. Stage 2: Implement call SDP encryption: wrap SDP offer/answer in envelope, unwrap on receive. Test: audio call (1:1, then group). Stage 3: Metrics: log call_e2ee_enabled per-call, track failed/successful ratio. Stage 4: Progressive enable: set CALL_E2EE_ENABLED=0.5 (50% of users) via gradual rollout config, monitor 24h for crashes. Stage 5: If stable, ramp to 100% and remove flag (make default ON). Rollback: flip CALL_E2EE_KILLSWITCH=1, returns 503, frontend falls back to plaintext.

items.title: Envelope Mode Deferred — Backend Tables Ready, No Final Client Integration
items.currentState: Backend has chat_pending_envelopes + chat_pending_envelope_bodies tables (created ~2026-05-16, lines 1592-1651 in chat.php). Server supports storing encrypted envelopes instead of plaintext messages. Cron job cron-chat-envelope-gc.php exists to GC stale envelopes. BUT: frontend chat-conversation.js still sends plaintext via content field in chat_send; no call to alternative chat_envelope_send endpoint (which exists at line 14887). Plaintext path is hardcoded default.
items.rootCause: Multi-stage SQLite-first chat migration (Stage 5: encrypted envelope) planned but incomplete. Tasks #1024 + #1038 reference 'Sender Keys envelope wire' + 'Stage 5 encrypted envelope' as queued. Backend infrastructure for envelope_mode is live but frontend routing (when to use envelope vs plaintext) is undefined.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp: All messages go through Signal-encrypted envelopes by default. Server never sees plaintext. Multi-device: fanout to all recipient devices via separate envelope per (recipient_email, device_id) pair. Groups: Sender Key protocol (one encryption, all recipients can decrypt without fan-out on sender side). 1:1: Individual envelope per recipient device.
items.fixPlan: Stage 1: Wire chat_send to call chat_envelope_send when conversation.is_e2ee=true. Pass encrypted content + envelope metadata instead of plaintext. Stage 2: Implement envelope storage lifecycle: created_at, delivered_at (per device), expires_at (30d). Stage 3: Client-side: add envelope_mode flag to conversation model; on send, check flag and route to chat_envelope_send (not chat_send). Stage 4: Add 'switch to encrypted' migration: on first E2EE enable, set flag, new messages auto-envelope, old plaintext messages remain readable (server keeps both paths). Stage 5: QA: send msg before E2EE, enable E2EE, send msg after, receive on second device, verify both readable, old one unencrypted preview, new one locked icon.

items.title: Group Encryption — Sender Keys Not Wired, Falls Back to Per-Recipient Fan-Out
items.currentState: Frontend createEnvelopeV3 (lines 855-965 in e2e.js) normalizes recipient bundles into device list, loops over each device, encrypts separately, returns { envelopes: { 'email|device_id': {...} } }. This is per-recipient encryption (fan-out). Backend chat_send receives envelope JSON, stores as plaintext in message content. No Sender Key protocol (Signal's group optimization: single encryption, all recipients derive same MK via group ratchet).
items.rootCause: Sender Keys (task #1035) is in task list as 'completed' but not actually wired. Code does naive N recipients = N encryptions. Scales poorly for large groups (100 members = 100 envelopes). WhatsApp uses Sender Key to send 1 ciphertext, all members compute shared group SK via DH, reduces bandwidth + CPU.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp Signal Protocol: 1:1 uses X3DH (4-DH, per-recipient envelope). Groups: Sender Key (GKR — Group Key Ratchet). Sender computes group session key once (derived from group_id + sender_id + counter). Encrypts message once with this key. All members use same identity key mapping to compute the same group SK (no server fanout needed, bandwidth O(1) not O(n)). Sender's device publishes group_session_key in addition to identity + signed_prekey.
items.fixPlan: Stage 1: Define group_session_key backend schema (group_id, sender_id, session_counter, root_key). Stage 2: Implement group SK derivation in e2e.js: kdfGroupRootKey() generates stable group SK from (group_id, topic_id, members list hash). Stage 3: On group send: if conversation.type='group' && is_e2ee, compute group SK once, encrypt message once, wrap in envelope { group_session_key_id, ciphertext }. For receive: reconstruct group SK on recipient side, decrypt. Stage 4: Fallback to per-device for 1:1 (no group_id). Stage 5: QA group E2EE: add 3 members, send 1 msg, 1 envelope in DB (not 3), each member decrypts using group SK, can reply (sender ratchets counter).

items.title: Staged Re-Enable Plan — Safe Rollout with QA Gates
items.currentState: Currently: all direct conversations plaintext by default (opt-in to enable). No production users on E2EE. No metrics, no monitoring, no gradual rollout infrastructure.
items.rootCause: Decision to avoid multi-device lock UX problem deferred the rollout. No safety gates defined.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp: Default ON, always has been. Signal, Telegram: opt-in toggle (Secret Chats). iMessage: always ON. Rollout strategy: test internally → beta (TestFlight/Play beta) → canary (1% users) → ramp (5%, 25%, 100%).
items.fixPlan: QA Gate 1 (Internal QA, this week): (a) Set DEFAULT_E2EE=true locally. (b) Log in on 2 emulators, send encrypted msg, receive, verify decryption + read receipt. (c) Test 1:1 → group upgrade (add 3rd person, should downgrade to plaintext or fan-out). (d) Test key rotation: login on new emulator, restore key, re-encrypt old msg. Gate 2 (Beta, Play/TestFlight, week 2): Enable for 10% of beta testers, monitor: crashes, decryption errors, sync issues. Log [E2EE] errors to analytics. Gate 3 (Canary, week 3): Ramp to 1% prod users, monitor 24h. If error_rate < 0.1%, proceed. Gate 4 (Production, week 4): Ramp 5% → 25% → 100%, check user retention/complaints. Rollback: setenv DEFAULT_E2EE=false, ship OTA, all new conversations plaintext (old encrypted ones still readable via envelope unwrap).

items.title: Live location share updates are 5-minute heartbeat, stale by design
items.currentState: Frontend: LiveLocationHeartbeat fires every 5 minutes in foreground + AppState-triggered on app resume. Background: LiveLocationHeartbeat starts backgroundLocationTask which fires on OS-managed interval (5min time interval + 100m distance interval on Android, iOS batches every 5min). Both send to chat_friend_location_share_update endpoint. Backend: chat_friend_location_share_update writes ONLY to chat_friend_location_shares table (not chat_live_locations conversation context). Snap-map reads via chat_friends_map_shares endpoint which JOINs shares with grants. Updated_at timestamp recorded but no real-time WebSocket fanout to viewers.
items.rootCause: The 5-minute heartbeat cadence is intentional (WhatsApp parity comment in code) but stale for users who want instant tracking. No real-time push fanout: when sharer's app posts new coords, receivers don't get pinged—they only see fresh pin next time they poll snap-map (no server push trigger). Ping request system exists (chat_friend_location_ping) but it's pull-based: receiver must explicitly ping sharer, who then re-posts. No automatic update-triggered fanout to all viewers.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp live location: automatic significant-location-change detection (100m threshold via iOS CLLocationManager + Android LocationManager) fires updates instantly. Google Maps: 3-minute adaptive interval documented in support forums, adjusts based on movement. Find My (Apple): runs CLLocationManager.startLocationUpdatesAsync() with significant-change notification (~500m trigger), continuously in background. Common pattern: update event → server receives → broadcast via WebSocket/FCM to ALL viewers immediately (not pull-based). Sources: [Find My location handling](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/handling-location-updates-in-the-background), [Google Maps 3min interval](https://support.google.com/maps/thread/247860740), [iOS significant location](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/cllocationmanager/1423531-startmonitoringsignificantlocati), [WhatsApp live location](https://www.howtoisolve.com/whatsapp-live-location-everything-you-need-to-know-about/), [Real-time fanout architecture](https://codelit.io/blog/notification-system-architecture)
items.fixPlan: Stage 1 (quick win): Drop heartbeat from 5min to 30s foreground + 1min background (still respects quiet periods, less stale). Stage 2 (WhatsApp parity): Implement CLLocationManager.startLocationUpdatesAsync() with accuracy:Balanced + distanceFilter:100m (iOS triggers on 100m move, not time-based). Android: LocationManager.requestLocationUpdates(100m distance filter). Stage 3 (real-time fanout): On chat_friend_location_share_update POST, broadcast via WebSocket to all receivers with active grants: `{ type: 'live_location_update', sharer_email, lat, lng, accuracy, updated_at }` (not just update the PG row). Stage 4 (map auto-refresh): FrontEnd snap-map must listen to WS 'live_location_update' and re-render pin in real-time (don't wait for next poll). Stage 5 (battery): Reduce update rate when app backgrounded (2min instead of 1min) + pause entirely if user exits snap-map screen for >30s.

items.title: Ping-request system is one-way: receiver can ping sharer, but no auto-recovery
items.currentState: LiveLocationPingListener mounted at root layout listens to WS 'location_ping_request'. When fired, it calls Location.getCurrentPositionAsync() with Balanced accuracy (10s timeout), then POSTs to chat_friend_location_share_update. Backend chat_friend_location_ping endpoint fires silent FCM (via fcmSendSilentSync) + WS relay to sharer. Throttled 1 ping per 60s per (receiver, sharer) pair.
items.rootCause: Ping is only initiated when receiver actively calls chat_friend_location_ping (snaps map and user sees '23h stale' → taps to refresh). No automatic ping recovery: if sharer's app backgrounded for 12h and user never taps map refresh, sharer's pin stays frozen. No server-side 'is this pin stale?' check with auto-ping (24h+ without update should trigger auto-recovery).
items.whatsappPattern: Find My + WhatsApp don't have explicit 'ping' endpoints. Instead, they use continuous background monitoring: if device's location hasn't updated in >30min, the OS wakes the app + pings GPS (CLLocationManager), gets fresh fix, posts. Receiver side: map automatically refreshes when new coord arrives (via fanout push). No explicit 'user taps refresh' action needed. Sources: [iOS background location](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/handling-location-updates-in-the-background)
items.fixPlan: Wire server-side cron to detect stale shares: SELECT * FROM chat_friend_location_shares WHERE is_unlimited=TRUE AND updated_at < NOW()-30min. For each stale row, fire silent FCM ping to sharer + log for debugging (don't auto-revoke, just wake the app). Ensure background task handler checks share-active flag before posting (it already does at /root/webmail-app/services/backgroundLocationTask.js:64). Add metric: count of auto-woken pings per day.

items.title: Map render has no real-time push: snap-map rerenders only on manual poll or page-open
items.currentState: Snap-map reads chat_friends_map_shares on demand (user navigates to map tab or pulls refresh). No WebSocket listener for live_location_update events. Map re-renders entire pin list. Updated_at timestamp shown to user but not auto-updating.
items.rootCause: Frontend snap-map component has no WS subscription channel for live location updates. When sharer POSTs new coords, receiver's snap-map UI doesn't learn about it until next manual poll or app-restart. Snap-map is pull-only (chat_friends_map_shares endpoint).
items.whatsappPattern: Google Maps + WhatsApp + Find My: when location updates arrive, receiver's map automatically updates the pin position + timestamp. No manual refresh needed. Achieved via: (1) server broadcasts update to all connected receivers over WebSocket, (2) frontend listens to 'location_update' channel, (3) re-renders pin at new lat/lng. Sources: [Fan-out notification architecture](https://codelit.io/blog/notification-system-architecture)
items.fixPlan: Frontend: After snap-map mounts, subscribe to WS channel 'live_location:' + current_email (e.g., 'live_location:alice@chatyy.com'). Handler: on 'live_location_update' message, update in-memory pin state + re-render map (use Reanimated to animate pin smoothly across map). Backend: In chat_friend_location_share_update, after INSERT/UPDATE, call _broadcastFriendMapToUser(sharer_email, 'live_location_update', { ... }) to fanout to all viewers with active grants. Codebase already has _broadcastFriendMapToUser helper (used in ping endpoint); reuse it.

items.title: Background location task fires at OS-managed cadence (5min + 100m), not user-intended duration
items.currentState: backgroundLocationTask.startLocationUpdatesAsync() configured with: timeInterval 5min (Android hint), distanceInterval 100m, deferredUpdatesInterval 5min (iOS batching). Fires TaskManager task, posts to chat_friend_location_share_update. No correlation to user's selected duration (15min, 1h, 8h, unlimited).
items.rootCause: Expected behavior for iOS/Android background APIs: the OS controls frequency, not the app. User's '15min duration' is about when the share *expires* in the database, not about GPS update frequency.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp live location uses CLLocationManager.startLocationUpdatesAsync() + ActivityType.other + pausesUpdatesAutomatically: false (similar to Chatyy code). Actual update cadence is OS-managed, typically firing every few seconds to minutes depending on movement. User's duration selection (15m, 1h, 8h) is expiry time, NOT GPS frequency. Sources: [iOS location updates background](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/cllocationmanager/1620551-requestlocationupdates)
items.fixPlan: No change needed — current design is correct per iOS/Android OS constraints. Document in code comment: 'User-selected duration controls expires_at in DB, not GPS polling frequency.' To reduce battery: (1) increase distanceFilter from 100m → 300m on stationary detection (geofence API), (2) reduce deferredUpdatesInterval from 5min → 10min if user hasn't moved. Track in LiveLocationHeartbeat: if speed = 0 for >2min, call backgroundLocationTask.updateIntervalForStationary().

All event modifications require either: (a) tap → navigate to detail screen → edit form, or (b) swipe on list card → edit/delete. No direct drag-to-move, drag-to-resize, or drag-to-delete on the visual calendar itself. This is the primary UX gap: calendar editing requires leaving the month/week view instead of inline gesture.
items.whatsappPattern: WhatsApp Events (via Google Calendar integration): Desktop web shows drag-to-reschedule (drag event block to new time slot in week view, highlights drop zone, animates event). iOS native Apple Calendar: long-press event → swipe up/down to change time; drag event in month view → visual feedback (semi-transparent ghost image follows finger). Google Calendar: drag event in week/day view (desktop + web) → visual reordering. iOS: tap event → quick edit menu (no drag). Pattern: drag is primary on desktop/web (visual feedback); mobile prefers swipe + modal due to fat-finger risk.
items.fixPlan: PHASED APPROACH: Phase 1 (OTA): Enhance SwipeableEventCard to support swipe-up = quick-duration-picker (30min/1h/2h presets), swipe-down = reschedule modal. Phase 2 (native if needed): Add LongPressGestureHandler on WeekView event blocks → show 'drag to reschedule' affordance + semi-transparent duplicate block that follows finger during drag. Drop zone feedback (highlight potential time slot). Phase 3 (optional): Month view click → week view for that day (already navigates, no need for drag on dots). Implementation: Use react-native-gesture-handler if already in dependencies (check package.json); fallback to PanResponder for broader mobile compat. Animate ghost image + drop-zone highlight using Animated API (already used for other calendar animations).

items.title: One AI calling fails with 'we are sorry an application error occurred'
items.currentState: User requests a call via One AI. Frontend sends make_call action. Backend calls oneMakeCall() at /var/www/mail/api/one.php:3371, which: (1) loads Twilio creds from /etc/mail-api.env; (2) normalizes phone via oneNormalizePhone(); (3) generates TTS audio via oneGenerateCallAudio(); (4) makes HTTP POST to Twilio API with params To/From/Url/StatusCallback. Response handling at line 3438-3448: if HTTP 200-299 and data.sid present, returns {success: true}; else returns {error: msg}. Frontend error handling at app/one.js line 2451 stores result in allToolCalls[]. If error, the 'error' key is returned in JSON response, but frontend rendering at one.js appears to show generic 'application error' banner instead of the specific error message.
items.rootCause: Two potential root causes: (1) Twilio credentials missing/invalid in /etc/mail-api.env (TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER) — returns {error: 'Voice not configured'} at line 3384. (2) Phone number normalization fails (oneNormalizePhone returns falsy) — returns {error: 'Numero de telefone invalido...'} at line 3389. (3) TTS audio generation fails (oneGenerateCallAudio returns falsy) — no explicit check, proceeds with null $audioUrl. (4) HTTP curl error to Twilio API — returns {error: 'Failed to connect...'} at line 3435. (5) Twilio HTTP error response — returns {error: 'Call failed: ' . $errMsg} at line 3447. Frontend receives error but the user sees a generic error message instead of the specific reason.
items.fixPlan: 1. Add logging to oneMakeCall() to capture each failure point (missing creds, bad phone, TTS fail, Twilio HTTP error, curl error). 2. Verify /etc/mail-api.env exists and has TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER set with correct values. 3. Check oneNormalizePhone() logic (search /var/www/mail/api/one.php for its definition) to ensure it accepts international + national formats. 4. Check oneGenerateCallAudio() implementation — ensure it returns a valid URL or errors clearly. 5. Add explicit HTTP status logging and Twilio response body logging on >299 responses. 6. Frontend: surface the actual error message from the backend {error} field to the user instead of generic 'application error' banner.

Add explicit error logging in oneExecuteTool() switch statement to log the ACTUAL error from each tool instead of the generic 'Hmm, nao consegui fazer isso agora'. 4. Check redisRateCheck() for free users — is it rejecting legitimate requests? Log when rate limit fires. 5. Review the greeting fast-path logic at line 10030-10035 — ensure it's not TOO aggressive and clearing tools for intentional action requests. 6. Add a 'tools_available' field to the final response JSON so frontend can log/display which tools were available. 7. items.title: One AI conversation does not persist across app closes/reopens — loses history after <2 hours idle
items.currentState: Frontend: app/one.js uses AsyncStorage + cache to persist conversation ID and messages. On app open, useFocusEffect at line 1957 calls resetIfStale(), which checks a persisted lastActiveAt timestamp. If (now - lastActiveAt) >= ONE_RESET_WINDOW_MS (2 hours, line 1906), it clears the conversationId, messages[], and message cache. Then loadConversations() at line 1970 is called with autoRestore=true. If convos exist and the most recent was updated <2h ago (line 2021-2022), it sets conversationId to last.id and loads messages from backend. Backend: one_messages table stores role/content/tool_calls/tool_results per message, and one_conversations table stores id/user_email/title/updated_at. On app open, oneHistory() endpoint returns list of conversations. Issue: (1) onlyRECENT 30 conversations loaded (line 10326); (2) Persist logic depends on two independent timestamps (server updated_at + client lastActiveAt); (3) If timestamps disagree or parse incorrectly, the thread is discarded (new conversation created).
items.rootCause: Task #944 was supposed to implement 2h auto-new-conversation logic. According to the code comments at lines 1996-2006, there IS a bug: PG returns updated_at as TEXT without explicit timezone parsing. The old code evaluated 'NaN >= ONE_RESET_WINDOW_MS' which is ALWAYS false, falling through to restore the old thread. The NEW code (lines 2021-2022) intentionally fails SAFE on parse error by checking Number.isFinite(msAgo). However, looking closer, the code SHOULD work: if updated_at is unparseable, msAgo will be NaN, isStaleByServer will be true (line 2021), and the thread will NOT be restored — starting fresh instead. So the 2h reset is working as designed. The ROOT CAUSE of 'losing history' might be: (1) One_conversations table is being truncated/garbage-collected on the backend (no GC cron found in codebase). (2) Conversations are soft-deleted but frontend still tries to load them and gets 404. (3) PG updated_at is not being updated when the user sends a message (line 10291: UPDATE one_conversations SET updated_at=NOW() — appears to be there). (4) Message cache key mismatch ('one_messages_' + conversationId) — if conversationId changes, old messages are orphaned.
items.fixPlan: 1. Verify that one_conversations.updated_at IS being updated on every new message (line 10291) — add logging to confirm. 2. Check for any backend GC cron or cleanup job that might be deleting old conversations — search /var/www/mail/api/ for cron files or DELETE statements on one_conversations. 3. Test the full flow: (a) Start a conversation in One AI, send multiple messages. (b) Check one_conversations and one_messages tables that rows are created. (c) Close the app. (d) Wait 1 hour and reopen — should restore (still within 2h). (e) Wait 2+ hours and reopen — should start fresh (expected behavior). (f) Re-run test with 30+ conversations to ensure pagination works (not limited to 30). 4. Add logging to loadConversations() to show: (a) how many convos loaded from backend, (b) the updated_at timestamp of the most recent, (c) the parsed Date and msAgo value, (d) whether isStaleByServer/isStaleByLocal evaluated to true, (d) whether setConversationId was called. 5. Add a 'persistence_debug' endpoint to backend that returns last 5 convo IDs + updated_at + message count for a user — helps diagnose whether data is on the server. 6. Ensure frontend message cache key is stable and matches conversationId — no UUID collision possible.

items.title: Docs: Implementar sistema 'trabalhar com alguém' — Google Docs LIVE collab
items.currentState: Docs system exists (app/documentos.js, docs.php backend, WebView editors editor.html/spreadsheet.html). Basic sharing exists via docs_doc_shares table with view/edit/admin permissions. But editors work in isolation — no real-time delta sync, no presence tracking, no live broadcasts. Changes only merge on manual reload.
items.rootCause: Missing CRDT/OT engine. No WebSocket presence layer. No document delta API. No conflict-free merge strategy. Editors don't see each other's changes in real-time. syncRecordEvent notifies only via async event queue, not instant WS.
items.whatsappPattern: Google Docs (OT conflict-free + presence cursors) / Notion (Yjs CRDT + awareness awareness layer) pattern. Real-time delta sync (not full doc save), multiplexed WebSocket stream, user awareness with avatars + cursor overlay. Offline-first option: local Yjs store, reconnect syncs deltas. Alternative patterns: Firebase Realtime (proprietary), ShareDB (OT library, Node.js native).
items.fixPlan: STAGE 1: Add Yjs provider to Node WS infrastructure — create `docs_content_deltas` table (timestamp, user_email, doc_id, delta_data_json), GC old deltas (30d rolling). STAGE 2: Integrate Yjs into WebView editors (editor.html CKEditor + Yjs binding). Wire presence awareness (avatars, cursor overlay). STAGE 3: Backend API `docs_editors_list` (who's editing now), `docs_update_delta` (delta stream). STAGE 4: App UI shows sharing status + live editor indicators. STAGE 5: Stress-test 5-user simultaneous editing, handle offline reconnect.
